facts.fact: Yes: an NRI (adult or minor) with a valid Indian passport can apply for Aadhaar at any Aadhaar Enrolment Centre
facts.quote: Yes. An NRI (whether minor or adult) with a valid Indian Passport can apply for Aadhaar from any Aadhaar Enrolment Centre.

facts.fact: The 182-days residence condition does not apply to NRIs
facts.quote: In case of NRIs the residential condition of 182 days is not mandatory.

facts.fact: A valid Indian passport is mandatory as Proof of Identity for an NRI
facts.quote: A valid Indian Passport is mandatory as a Proof of Identity (PoI) for NRI applicants.

facts.fact: Email ID is mandatory for NRIs; mobile number is optional
facts.quote: Optional demographic information (mobile number, email [mandatory for NRI and Resident Foreign National])

facts.fact: Biometrics are captured at enrolment: photo, 10 fingerprints and both irises
facts.quote: And Biometric Information (Photo, 10 finger prints, both Iris) Type of documents presented [valid Indian passport is mandatory as Proof of Identity (PoI)]

facts.fact: Enrolment needs a personal visit to an Aadhaar Enrolment Centre because biometrics are captured; there is no online enrolment
facts.quote: No, you have to personally visit Aadhaar Enrolment Centre for getting yourself enrolled as your biometrics will be captured.

facts.fact: Aadhaar centres are in India (Aadhaar Seva Kendras across India and Aadhaar Kendras run by banks, post offices, BSNL and state governments)
facts.quote: UIDAI has opened Aadhaar Seva Kendra in 78 districts across India. These include dedicated centres in all metro cities, all state capitals and Union Territories. These ASK will run along with over 66,000 Aadhaar Kendra already being run by banks, post offices, BSNL and state governments.
facts.note: UIDAI pages describe centres only in India; no enrolment facility abroad is published on uidai.gov.in (your-aadhaar and enrolment-and-update FAQs have no mention of enrolment outside India). WebSearch budget was exhausted on 28 Oct, so no wider search was possible.

facts.fact: An appointment can be booked and the nearest enrolment centre located on the myAadhaar portal (Book an Appointment, Locate Enrolment Center)
facts.quote: Few services like QR code scan, Book an Appointment, Order Aadhaar PVC card, Check Enrolment status, Locate Enrolment Center, File a complaint etc. can be accessed without registered mobile number on myAadhaar portal.

facts.fact: An NRI can enrol with the foreign address recorded in the passport
facts.quote: Yes, NRIs having recorded address out-side India in their passport can enroll for Aadhaar with the foreign address using form number 2 or 4 or 6 as the case may be.

facts.fact: Or the NRI can give any Indian address supported by a valid Proof of Address from UIDAI's list
facts.quote: You may choose to give any other Indian Address with a valid supporting Proof of Address (PoA) as per the list of documents acceptable by UIDAI

facts.fact: An NRI enrolled with an address outside India receives a password-protected e-Aadhaar by email
facts.quote: NRI enrolled with address out-side India will receive password protected e-Aadhaar along with password to open the attachment to their registered email id provided at the time of enrolment.

facts.fact: New enrolment is free of charge
facts.quote: acknowledgement slip containing the applicable charges (New Enrolment is Free of charge)

summary: All NRI enrolment facts confirmed on UIDAI's Your Aadhaar and Enrolment & Update FAQs (passport mandatory, 182 days not applicable, email mandatory, in-person visit, foreign or Indian address, e-Aadhaar by email, free).
